summary: Two airliners collided over the Grand Canyon in uncontrolled airspace; the disaster led directly to the creation of the FAA.
Failed to get airborne from a slush-covered runway on a third takeoff attempt; victims included eight Manchester United players (the Munich air disaster).
Collided over Staten Island in poor visibility; wreckage fell on Brooklyn and killed six people on the ground.
An elevator trim motor fault forced a rejected takeoff too late to stop; most victims were Atlanta arts patrons on a charter.
Broke apart in severe clear-air turbulence in the lee of Mount Fuji shortly after leaving Tokyo.
Struck a hillside on approach in rain and fog; victims included the Marshall University football team.
Charter carrying a rugby team struck a ridge in cloud; 16 survivors were rescued after 72 days in the mountains.
The crew fixated on a burned-out landing gear light while the autopilot was nudged off and the jet descended into the Everglades.
The rear cargo door blew out and the collapsing floor severed the control cables; deadliest crash in history at the time.
Flew into severe windshear from a thunderstorm microburst on final approach to JFK.
The KLM 747 began its takeoff roll in fog without clearance and struck the Pan Am 747 taxiing on the runway; deadliest accident in aviation history.
The captain became spatially disoriented at night after an attitude indicator failed shortly after takeoff from Bombay.
Circled with a landing gear problem until the tanks ran dry; the accident triggered modern crew resource management training.
The left engine separated on takeoff due to a faulty maintenance shortcut and damaged the wing; two people on the ground also died. Deadliest crash on US soil.
A cargo hold fire broke out after takeoff; the aircraft landed intact but no evacuation began and everyone aboard died of smoke and fire.
Took off with ice on the wings and engine probes and anti-ice off; struck the 14th Street Bridge and fell into the Potomac River, killing four motorists too.
All four engines flamed out after flying through volcanic ash from Mount Galunggung at night; the crew restarted them and landed safely.
Ran out of fuel at cruise after a metric conversion error during refuelling; glided to a dead-stick landing at a former airbase (the Gimli Glider).
Strayed into Soviet airspace after an autopilot setup error and was shot down by an interceptor.
Destroyed by a bomb planted by Babbar Khalsa militants en route from Montreal to London; the deadliest bombing of a civilian airliner.
Flew into a microburst on final approach and hit a car on a highway, killing its driver; led to onboard windshear detection systems.
The aft pressure bulkhead ruptured because of a faulty repair years earlier, tearing off the vertical stabilizer and all hydraulics; deadliest single-aircraft accident ever.
Stalled just after takeoff, most likely from ice contamination on the wings; the dead included 248 US soldiers returning home.
The crew skipped the taxi checklist and took off without flaps or slats; a four-year-old girl was the only survivor and two people on the ground died.
An uncontrolled fire in the main-deck cargo area brought the jet down into the sea while diverting to Mauritius.
Fatigue cracks caused explosive decompression that peeled off part of the fuselage roof; a flight attendant was lost but the aircraft landed.
Shot down by missiles from the USS Vincennes, which misidentified the airliner as a fighter during a naval engagement.
Destroyed by a bomb in the forward cargo hold; falling wreckage killed 11 residents of Lockerbie.
A fan blade broke up in the left engine and the crew mistakenly shut down the healthy right one; crashed on a motorway embankment short of the runway.
An uncontained tail-engine failure destroyed all three hydraulic systems; the crew steered with engine thrust alone and 184 people survived the crash landing.
Ran out of fuel after long holding delays and a missed approach at JFK; the crew never declared a formal fuel emergency to ATC.
Rolled and dived on final approach after an uncommanded rudder hardover; the cause took investigators years to pin down.
A thrust reverser deployed in flight at cruise, causing loss of control and an in-flight breakup.
The crew fought the autopilot after accidentally triggering go-around mode; the jet pitched up, stalled and crashed on landing.
Autopilot yaw and roll wiring had been cross-connected during maintenance, causing violent oscillations and breakup in flight.
A rudder servo valve jam caused a rudder reversal and loss of control on approach; led to a fleet-wide 737 rudder redesign.
Descended into a mountain at night after a navigation database mix-up and loss of situational awareness during a rushed approach.
Expired chemical oxygen generators loaded improperly as cargo ignited a fierce fire in the hold minutes after takeoff.
The centre fuel tank exploded, most likely ignited by a wiring short circuit; led to fuel tank inerting requirements.
The deadliest mid-air collision in history, near Delhi, after the Il-76 descended below its assigned level.
Struck a hill on a night approach with the glideslope out of service; cockpit hierarchy and fatigue were cited.
Dived from cruise into a river; US investigators concluded deliberate pilot action while Indonesian investigators left the cause undetermined.

location: off Peggy's Cove Nova Scotia Canada
summary: An in-flight fire spread from wiring above the cockpit, linked to the entertainment system; crashed into the Atlantic during a diversion to Halifax.
The NTSB attributed the dive to deliberate control inputs by the relief first officer; Egyptian authorities disputed the finding.
The horizontal stabilizer trim jackscrew failed from missed lubrication; the jet pitched over and dived inverted into the sea.
A metal strip on the runway burst a tyre and debris ruptured a fuel tank on takeoff; four people died on the ground and Concorde never recovered commercially.
Hijacked by al-Qaeda terrorists and flown into the North Tower of the World Trade Center.
Hijacked and flown into the South Tower of the World Trade Center.
Hijacked and flown into the Pentagon; 125 people inside the building also died.
Hijacked; passengers fought back and the aircraft crashed in a field short of its intended target.
The vertical stabilizer snapped off after aggressive rudder inputs in wake turbulence; five people on the ground also died.
Broke apart at cruise from metal fatigue traced to an improper repair after a tailstrike 22 years earlier.
Collided at night after an overloaded controller and TCAS gave conflicting instructions; most victims were Russian schoolchildren.
Cabin pressurization was left in manual after maintenance; everyone aboard was incapacitated by hypoxia and the jet flew on until fuel ran out.
Attempted takeoff from a short unlit runway at dawn; the first officer was the sole survivor.
Clipped over the Amazon by a business jet whose transponder was inactive; the 737 broke up in flight while the smaller jet landed.
Overran a wet runway at Congonhas with one thrust reverser deactivated and hit a warehouse; 12 people on the ground also died.
Took off without flaps or slats after checklist omissions; the takeoff configuration warning never sounded.
Lost both engines to Canada geese after takeoff from LaGuardia; Captain Sullenberger ditched on the Hudson and everyone survived.
The captain responded incorrectly to a stall warning on approach to Buffalo; one person in a house also died. Reshaped US pilot experience rules.
The pitot tubes iced over at cruise and the crew held the aircraft in a stall they never recognized until impact.
Descended below minimums in thick fog and struck trees; the dead included President Lech Kaczynski and much of Poland's leadership.
Landed long and fast on Mangalore's tabletop runway and plunged into a gorge; eight passengers survived.
Struck the Margalla Hills in monsoon cloud during a mishandled circling approach; the deadliest crash on Pakistani soil.
An uncontained engine failure shredded wiring and systems across the wing; the crew worked through dozens of failures and landed safely.
Struck the seawall short of the runway after the crew let the speed decay on a visual approach.
Vanished en route from Kuala Lumpur to Beijing after turning off course; the main wreckage has never been found.
Shot down over eastern Ukraine by a Buk surface-to-air missile brought in from Russia.
A cracked solder joint kept faulting the rudder limiter; the crew's response cut out the autopilot and the jet stalled from cruise.
One engine auto-feathered after takeoff and the crew shut down the working one; clipped a bridge on dashcam video before hitting the river.
The first officer locked the captain out of the cockpit and flew the aircraft into a mountainside.
Destroyed by a bomb placed aboard at Sharm El Sheikh; the ISIS Sinai branch claimed the attack.
Crashed en route from Paris to Cairo; evidence points to an in-flight fire near the cockpit though the findings remain disputed.
Hit the runway during a go-around attempted without takeoff thrust; all 300 aboard evacuated the burning jet but a firefighter died.
Ran out of fuel minutes from landing after skipping a planned stop; victims included most of Brazil's Chapecoense football team.
A fatigued fan blade failed and debris smashed a cabin window, causing decompression; one passenger died and the jet landed in Philadelphia.
A leased jet stalled and crashed shortly after takeoff; investigators cited crew errors in weight and balance calculations.
MCAS repeatedly pushed the nose down on faulty angle-of-attack data; the first of the two 737 MAX disasters.
MCAS activated on bad sensor data after takeoff from Addis Ababa; the MAX fleet was grounded worldwide days later.
Returned after a lightning strike, landed hard and bounced; the gear punched into the fuel tanks and the rear cabin burned.
Shot down by Iranian air defence missiles minutes after takeoff amid heightened military tensions.
Overran the tabletop runway at Calicut in heavy rain and broke apart in a gorge; both pilots were among the dead.
An autothrottle fault created asymmetric thrust after takeoff; the crew lost control and the jet dived into the sea.
Dived from cruise into a mountainside; no final report has been released, with reporting pointing to deliberate control inputs.
Both propellers were inadvertently feathered on approach when the crew moved the condition levers instead of the flaps.
The A350 struck a Coast Guard turboprop that had entered the runway; all 379 aboard the airliner evacuated while five Coast Guard crew died.
Entered a flat spin and fell almost vertically after severe icing at altitude; Brazil's deadliest crash since 2007.
Damaged by Russian air defence fire near Grozny and crashed while diverting across the Caspian; 29 people survived.
Suffered a bird strike on approach, belly-landed without gear and overran into a concrete localizer mound; two crew in the tail survived.
A regional jet on final to Reagan National collided with an Army helicopter over the Potomac; no one on either aircraft survived.

Crashed into a medical college hostel seconds after takeoff; the preliminary report centred on both engine fuel control switches moving to cutoff. One passenger survived and 19 people died on the ground.
The left engine and pylon separated during takeoff and the freighter crashed into businesses beyond the runway; people on the ground were also killed.
